evidence.title: Harnessing the Power of Microwave Irradiation: A Novel Approach to Bitumen Partial Upgrading.
evidence.abstract: The partial upgrading of "tar-like" Canadian bitumen is an essential process to reduce its viscosity to an acceptable range that meets the required pipeline specifications. An innovative and potentially greener solution has emerged in the form of microwave irradiation. This work proposes and demonstrates the use of an electrically powered commercial microwave along with carbon-based microwave susceptors (activated carbon, biochar, coke, and graphite) to promote localized thermal cracking within bitumen at a temperature as low as 150 °C, compared to the conventional method of 400 °C. The remarkable results show that just 0.1 wt% of carbon additives can reduce the viscosity of bitumen by 96% with just 10 min of microwaving at 200 °C. A Saturates, Aromatics, Resins, and Asphaltenes (SARA) analysis reveals that the mass fractions of light components (saturates) are almost doubled and that almost one-third of heavy polar hydrocarbon constituents are cracked and decomposed into much lighter molecules, resulting in higher-quality, less viscous bitumen. Furthermore, this study highlights the key role of the surface area and porosity of the carbon microwave susceptor in absorbing microwave radiation, offering exciting new avenues for optimization. Microwave-assisted partial upgrading of bitumen is a cost-effective and eco-friendly alternative to conventional upgrading, producing upgraded bitumen that requires significantly less diluent at a lower cost prior to pipeline transportation.

evidence.title: Microwave Electro-technological Installation for Processing Vegetable-origin Organic Materials and Agricultural Crops
evidence.abstract: The research aims to conduct experimental studies of the drying schedule for processing vegetable-origin organic materials using a microwave electro-technological installation. The design and development of a microwave electro-technological installation for processing vegetable-origin organic materials and agricultural crops are based on the solution of an agreed boundary value problem of electrodynamics and heat and mass transfer. The experiments on the microwave processing of vegetable-origin organic materials using a microwave electro-technological installation allowed us to identify the preferred process conditions, which involve the work of 7 magnetrons and a rotation mechanism of vegetable-origin organic materials along their axis. The processing time is less than 15 hours; the final humidity does not exceed 7%. The temperature change is uniform. The temperature at a depth of 1/4 of the thickness of the samples differs from the temperature on the surface of the samples by 0.5–1.0°C. The differences in the calculated and experimental data on the humidity of organic materials of plant origin do not exceed 3.8%, and on temperature, it is 4.3%. The creation of a microwave installation for the simultaneous microwave processing of vegetable organic materials and agricultural crops will significantly increase the energy and economic efficiency of the installation by reducing the processing time and increasing the quality of dried material quality. Moreover, unlike the existing ones, the proposed electro-technological installation contributes to the sale of more than two products with improved qualities, thus increasing the profits at the same energy costs.

evidence.title: Rejuvenated Graphene Nanoplatelets Unlocking Extrinsic Self-Healing in Asphalt Binders.
evidence.abstract: The aging and fatigue susceptibility of asphalt binders significantly reduce the pavement service life. This work presents a multifunctional strategy to enhance binder durability through the development of rejuvenated graphene nanoplatelets (GnP-Rej), where a vegetable-oil-based rejuvenator is intercalated within graphene nanoplatelets, enabling microwave-activated self-healing. Structural and thermal characterizations using Fourier Transformed Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman Spectroscopy (RS), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), and Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) confirmed successful rejuvenator's intercalation with the graphene nanoplatelets via noncovalent interactions. Additionally, rheological tests revealed that low-to-moderate neat GnP contents (0.1-0.18 wt %) improved rutting resistance (G*/sin(δ)), with microwave treatment further enhancing binder flexibility via improved rejuvenator diffusion. Fatigue testing using Linear Amplitude Sweep (LAS) method showed that microwave-activated rejuvenated graphene nanoplatelets (GnP-Rej_MW) formulations, particularly at 0.24 wt %, significantly extended fatigue life and reduced strain sensitivity (lowest B = 3.39), outperforming untreated counterparts. 2.2.3. Multiple Stress Creep Recovery (MSCR) results confirmed these findings, with 0.1-0.18 wt % GnP-Rej_MW binders demonstrating the best balance of deformation resistance (low Jnr) and elastic recovery (high R3.2%). Healing analysis revealed that microwave-activated binders with 0.18-0.24 wt % GnP-Rej achieved Healing Index (HI) above 1.4, confirming effective stiffness recovery and self-healing behavior. Overall, the combination of graphene nanoplatelets, biobased rejuvenator, and microwave activation provides a scalable route to smart, self-healing asphalt binders. These materials offer a promising solution for extending pavement lifespan while reducing maintenance frequency and cost.

evidence.title: High-Efficiency Ultrajet Hydrodynamic Cracking of Heavy Bitumen and Oil Sludge
evidence.abstract: This study investigates the efficiency of ultrajet hydrodynamic treatment for the cracking of highly viscous bitumens and oil sludges. Experiments were conducted using a high-pressure Flow JetForce HHP-500 installation capable of generating jets with velocities of up to 820 m/s and pressures up to 320 MPa. The research analyzed the effects of jet velocity, impact angle, cyclic flow modes, and turbulence-enhancing inserts on viscosity reduction and the yield of light fractions. After two processing cycles with maximum parameters, the viscosity decreased by 65% (from 9100 to 3100 ± 150 mPa s, n = 3 at 25 °C), and the yield of fractions with Tboil < 350 °C increased to 33.5 ± 1.0 p.p. (n = 3). Cyclic feeding and turbulence added another 3–4 p.p. to the yield without a noticeable increase in specific energy capacity. The study also showed that compared to ultrasonic cavitation and thermal pyrolysis, ultrajet processing achieved comparable or superior results while consuming significantly less energy and shorter processing times. The findings confirm that the ultrajet hydrodynamic technology represents a promising, energy-efficient approach for upgrading heavy hydrocarbons and reducing processing complexity.

mechanism_map.mechanism: Carbon-based microwave susceptors absorb microwave energy and convert it into localized thermal energy, with uptake governed by the susceptor's surface area and porosity, enabling targeted heating at lower bulk power.
mechanism_map.intervention: Install a food-safe, high-surface-area carbon-loaded susceptor plate/sleeve inside the countertop cavity, positioned beneath and around the food, so it preferentially captures microwave energy from the standing-wave field and re-emits it as evenly distributed conductive/radiant heat into the food center, flattening the hot-edge/cold-center gradient with no user stirring.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Markedly lower spatial temperature non-uniformity across the load (edges no longer burn while the center stays cold), achieved passively within the existing countertop form factor and a standard single cycle.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Heat a fixed reference load (e.g., 200 g starch gel in a shallow Petri dish) at rated power for 60 s with and without the susceptor plate; map surface temperature by IR thermography and center temperature by fiber-optic probe, then compute max−min ΔT and spatial standard deviation; the mechanism is falsified if ΔT is not reduced by at least 30% or if edge temperature still exceeds center temperature by more than 10 °C.

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: The partial upgrading of "tar-like" Canadian bitumen is an essential process to reduce its viscosity to an acceptable range that meets the required pipeline specifications. An innovative and potentially greener solution has emerged in the form of microwave irradiation. This work proposes and demonstrates the use of an electrically powered commercial microwave along with carbon-based microwave susceptors (activated carbon, biochar, coke, and graphite) to promote localized thermal cracking within bitumen at a temperature as low as 150 °C, compared to the conventional method of 400 °C. The remarkable results show that just 0.1 wt% of carbon additives can reduce the viscosity of bitumen by 96% with just 10 min of microwaving at 200 °C. A Saturates, Aromatics, Resins, and Asphaltenes (SARA) analysis reveals that the mass fractions of light components (saturates) are almost doubled and that almost one-third of heavy polar hydrocarbon constituents are cracked and decomposed into much lighter molecules, resulting in higher-quality, less viscous bitumen. Furthermore, this study highlights the key role of the surface area and porosity of the carbon microwave susceptor in absorbing microwave radiation, offering exciting new avenues for optimization. Microwave-assisted partial upgrading of bitumen is a cost-effective and eco-friendly alternative to conventional upgrading, producing upgraded bitumen that requires significantly less diluent at a lower cost prior to pipeline transportation.

custody_records.raw_content: The research aims to conduct experimental studies of the drying schedule for processing vegetable-origin organic materials using a microwave electro-technological installation. The design and development of a microwave electro-technological installation for processing vegetable-origin organic materials and agricultural crops are based on the solution of an agreed boundary value problem of electrodynamics and heat and mass transfer. The experiments on the microwave processing of vegetable-origin organic materials using a microwave electro-technological installation allowed us to identify the preferred process conditions, which involve the work of 7 magnetrons and a rotation mechanism of vegetable-origin organic materials along their axis. The processing time is less than 15 hours; the final humidity does not exceed 7%. The temperature change is uniform. The temperature at a depth of 1/4 of the thickness of the samples differs from the temperature on the surface of the samples by 0.5–1.0°C. The differences in the calculated and experimental data on the humidity of organic materials of plant origin do not exceed 3.8%, and on temperature, it is 4.3%. The creation of a microwave installation for the simultaneous microwave processing of vegetable organic materials and agricultural crops will significantly increase the energy and economic efficiency of the installation by reducing the processing time and increasing the quality of dried material quality. Moreover, unlike the existing ones, the proposed electro-technological installation contributes to the sale of more than two products with improved qualities, thus increasing the profits at the same energy costs.

This work presents a multifunctional strategy to enhance binder durability through the development of rejuvenated graphene nanoplatelets (GnP-Rej), where a vegetable-oil-based rejuvenator is intercalated within graphene nanoplatelets, enabling microwave-activated self-healing. Structural and thermal characterizations using Fourier Transformed Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman Spectroscopy (RS), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), and Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) confirmed successful rejuvenator's intercalation with the graphene nanoplatelets via noncovalent interactions. Additionally, rheological tests revealed that low-to-moderate neat GnP contents (0.1-0.18 wt %) improved rutting resistance (G*/sin(δ)), with microwave treatment further enhancing binder flexibility via improved rejuvenator diffusion. Fatigue testing using Linear Amplitude Sweep (LAS) method showed that microwave-activated rejuvenated graphene nanoplatelets (GnP-Rej_MW) formulations, particularly at 0.24 wt %, significantly extended fatigue life and reduced strain sensitivity (lowest B = 3.39), outperforming untreated counterparts. 2.2.3. Multiple Stress Creep Recovery (MSCR) results confirmed these findings, with 0.1-0.18 wt % GnP-Rej_MW binders demonstrating the best balance of deformation resistance (low Jnr) and elastic recovery (high R3.2%). Healing analysis revealed that microwave-activated binders with 0.18-0.24 wt % GnP-Rej achieved Healing Index (HI) above 1.4, confirming effective stiffness recovery and self-healing behavior. Overall, the combination of graphene nanoplatelets, biobased rejuvenator, and microwave activation provides a scalable route to smart, self-healing asphalt binders. These materials offer a promising solution for extending pavement lifespan while reducing maintenance frequency and cost.

Experiments were conducted using a high-pressure Flow JetForce HHP-500 installation capable of generating jets with velocities of up to 820 m/s and pressures up to 320 MPa. The research analyzed the effects of jet velocity, impact angle, cyclic flow modes, and turbulence-enhancing inserts on viscosity reduction and the yield of light fractions. (n = 3). Cyclic feeding and turbulence added another 3–4 p.p. to the yield without a noticeable increase in specific energy capacity. The study also showed that compared to ultrasonic cavitation and thermal pyrolysis, ultrajet processing achieved comparable or superior results while consuming significantly less energy and shorter processing times. The findings confirm that the ultrajet hydrodynamic technology represents a promising, energy-efficient approach for upgrading heavy hydrocarbons and reducing processing complexity.
